title: Two-proportion test
biology: Heat survival in evolved and ancestral yeast
design: Independent cultures assigned to one genotype; survival is scored once.
data_characteristics: Binary survival in two independent groups
Known number of trials in each group
The target is a difference in survival probabilities
question: Does survival probability differ between evolved and ancestral yeast?
null: Evolved and ancestral cultures have equal survival probabilities.
options: List successes and totals in the same group order.
correct = FALSE uses the uncorrected large-sample test.
The CI follows the first-minus-second group order.
assumptions: Expected cell counts support the large-sample approximation.
Use trials, not percentages without denominators.
parametric: Use logistic regression to adjust for temperature or batch.
Use a binomial mixed model when cultures share batches.
nonparametric: Use Fisher exact inference for sparse 2 × 2 tables.
Permutation of group labels requires exchangeable independent cultures.

plot_args.note: Use filled symbols and restrained group colors.

code_simulate:
set.seed(3103)
d <- data.frame(group = rep(c("Evolved", "Ancestral"), each = 110))
d$survived <- rbinom(220, 1, rep(c(.72, .52), each = 110))
write.csv(d, file.path(out_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
par(mar = c(4, 5, 2, 1), las = 1)
plot(1:2, estimate, xlim = c(.5, 2.5), ylim = c(0, 1),
     xaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "Survival probability", bty = "n",
     pch = 21, bg = c("#126887", "#b96735"), cex = 2.2)
arrows(1:2, group_ci[1, ], 1:2, group_ci[2, ],
       code = 3, angle = 90, length = .1, lwd = 2)
axis(1, 1:2, groups)
mtext("Intervals describe each probability; test the difference directly.", 3,
      cex = .85, col = "#555555")
code_analysis:
groups <- c("Evolved", "Ancestral")
x <- sapply(groups, function(g) sum(d$survived[d$group == g]))
n <- sapply(groups, function(g) sum(d$group == g))
fit <- prop.test(x, n, correct = FALSE)
estimate <- x / n
difference <- estimate[1] - estimate[2]
ci <- fit$conf.int
group_ci <- sapply(1:2, function(i) prop.test(x[i], n[i],
                                            correct = FALSE)$conf.int)
practice: If the groups contain 20 and 200 cultures, why are their denominators essential?
generating_model: Generate 110 independent evolved cultures and 110 independent ancestral cultures. Survival is Bernoulli with probabilities 0.72 and 0.52, respectively. No batching or pairing is introduced.
generating_truth: Evolved minus ancestral survival probability is 0.20, so the equal-probabilities null is false. The corresponding population odds ratio is approximately 2.37.
teaching_point: Keep group order explicit: the contrast is evolved minus ancestral, and its confidence interval addresses the actual comparison.
